outcome.answer: Large language models can turn conversational data into structured preference triples, link them to knowledge-base entities, and use the resulting personal knowledge graph for recommendations; one evaluated pipeline found that some lightweight models’ extraction quality tracked downstream recommendation utility [2]. Another approach uses LLMs to generate semantic profiles for knowledge-graph entities, integrates those profiles into the graph, and matches profile-based preferences during recommendation training [1]. For session-based recommendations, a heterogeneous graph can combine interactions, item relations, features, and metadata; learned user personas and LLM-derived item embeddings then inform candidate generation and reranking [3].
